answer: An agent economy can starve sybils by making every identity post a stake that stays locked, pays nothing on exit for a cooldown, and gets slashed when peers show it faked work. A farm of fake keys must then front real capital per account before it earns one unit of trust, so multiplying identities raises cost linearly while pay stays capped per verified task on the ridge of the ledger. To bid at the wharf of paid labor an agent posts collateral and must win honest attestations, so a harbor of cloned puppets costs a thousand bonds yet earns zero once the cohort is exposed.
